title: lwdidR — project notes for Claude
text: R implementation Lee & Wooldridge panel estimator: residualize unit’s outcome using pre-treatment observations (demean / detrend / demeanq / detrendq), run pooled cross-sectional OLS residualized outcome. R port original Stata lwdid command (Soo Jeong Lee & Jeffrey M. Wooldridge, https://github.com/Soo-econ/lwdid). Two estimator families live behind one entry point, lwdid(): Small-N path (default, method = NULL) — Lee & Wooldridge (2026b, SSRN 5325686). Pooled cross-sectional OLS ydot_postavg, homoskedastic/HC1/HC3/cluster SEs distribution-free wild-cluster-bootstrap / permutation inference. whole original package (v0.1.x). Implemented R/lwdid.R, R/transform.R, R/estimate.R, R/staggered.R, R/methods.R. Large-N path (method = "ra"/"ipw"/"ipwra") — Lee & Wooldridge (2026a, JBES, doi:10.1080/07350015.2026.2683047). Added v0.2.0. Estimates ATT(g,t) per cohort × calendar period via regression adjustment / IPW / doubly-robust IPWRA, aggregates (treated-count-weighted) event-study WATT(r) path plus Pre/Post averages, wild-cluster-bootstrap SEs sup-t simultaneous confidence bands. Implemented R/large_n.R, R/transform_large.R, R/estimators_large.R, R/aggregate_large.R, R/inference_large.R, R/methods_large.R, R/plot_large.R. Result class c("lwdid_large", "lwdid"). paths ported line--line Stata lwdid v2.4.2’s .ado/Mata source (see file-header comments R/*_large.R file approximate source line ranges) — reimplementation papers alone, faithful transcription, doubt intended behavior, fidelity target Stata’s code, plausible-looking rewrite.

title: lwdidR — project notes for Claude
text: easiest thing get backwards. lwdid() accepts post column common-timing designs, can mean two different things: post = D_it, treatment-indicator (1 treated units post periods, 0 everywhere else including periods control units). original/backwards-compatible behavior: dvar needed. ever_post units (row post==1) inferred treated group. post = calendar indicator (1 units, treated control alike, t >= first treated period; 0 ). case treatment status lives separate column, MUST either pass via dvar = "treated" unambiguous unit-invariant 0/1 column named exactly treat, treated, D, d data (auto-detected). lwdid() disambiguates automatically checking, calendar period, whether post takes single value across units — periods “mixed” (0s 1s t), post used D_it (case 1); post constant--period takes 0 1 across different periods, ’s calendar indicator (case 2), dvar resolution kicks (see R/lwdid.R lines ~204-242, .post_cal_ internal column). build calendar-post dataset without obvious treat-like column without passing dvar, lwdid() throws rather guessing — deliberate, “fix” picking default. Internally, regardless case applies, lwdid() builds .post_cal_ column (t >= tpost1 every unit) calling apply_transform(), control units need ydot_postavg computed (post column may -0 case 1) can appear firstpost cross-section used estimate_att().

title: lwdidR — project notes for Claude
text: Anchoring mechanical, estimated. large-N path, transformed outcome forced exactly 0 normalization period(s): r == -1 demean, r %% c(-2, -1) detrend (R/transform_large.R). propagates WATT(r) (.aggregate_large() hard-codes watt = 0 .inference_large() hard-codes se = 0 r) — future change one anchor list without matching change two files silently break sup-t band construction (anchor’s SE=0 column stays IF_r unpermuted). IPW-excludes covariates outcome model. method = "ipw", .fit_cell_large() sets xc_out <- NULL — covariates enter logit propensity score, never outcome-model regressors (mirrors Stata’s reg yvar dvar_g [aw=ipw] x terms). ra/ipwra, covariates cohort-centered (v - mean(v among first-treated--g), computed lwdid_large()) entering xc interaction d. Control-group membership cell (g,t) depends whether t pre post cohort’s treatment, never (R/large_n.R lines ~66-72): pre-period cells (tt < g) include -yet cohorts unconditionally (gv > g); post-period cells additionally require gv > tt (cohort already switched tt serve control). Getting backwards silently contaminates control group already-treated units post periods. Overall ATT (small-N staggered) naive average cohort ATTs. one pooled OLS: treated unit contributes -cohort ydot_postavg; never-treated unit contributes treated-count-weighted average ydot_postavg across cohorts serve control . README explicitly flags yields SE ≈ 0.061, 0.051 delta-method averaging — future refactor lwdid_staggered() “simplifies” two-stage average, quietly change SE break Castle Doctrine replication numbers. prepare_controls() silently drops controls, warning(), N1 <= K+1 N0 <= K+1 firstpost/period cross-section (R/estimate.R). silently-underpowered cell period--period small-N regression can pass without error — check warnings interpreting att_by_period/att_by_cohort_time thin panels. detrend/detrendq require >= 2 pre-periods per unit (small-N path errors informatively; large-N path instead sets unit’s ydot NA whole panel rather erroring, cohorts mix short- long-history units silently lose short-history units estimation rather failing). pre (large-N ) restricts pre-window pre recent pre-periods ([g - pre, g - 1]); -1 (default) uses full pre-history. real Stata-parity option validated _pre3 reference config, dead code — don’t assume “pre-periods always better” tuning ; trades bias (longer trend/level window) variance susceptibility earlier confounding shocks. Field naming across two paths inconsistent design (bug “fix”): small-N staggered results use att/se/ci_lower/ci_upper; large-N results use watt/se/lower_ci/upper_ci plus se_analytic. genuinely different objects (class = "lwdid" vs c("lwdid_large","lwdid")) different print/summary methods (R/methods.R vs R/methods_large.R) — don’t try unify column names without checking every caller.

M. (2026b). Simple Approaches Inference Difference--Differences Estimators Small Cross-Sectional Sample Sizes. Working paper, SSRN 5325686. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5325686 outcome transformation underlying estimator introduced (2026a); small-sample inference options (wild cluster bootstrap, permutation) staggered Castle Doctrine application replicated come (2026b). lwdidR R port original Stata lwdid command Soo Jeong Lee Jeffrey M. Wooldridge (https://github.com/Soo-econ/lwdid), whose v1.0 based (2026b). key idea simple: residualize unit’s outcome using pre-treatment observations, either demeaning detrending, run pooled cross-sectional OLS. package supports: - Common-timing staggered adoption designs - Transformation methods: demean, detrend, demeanq, detrendq - Standard errors: homoskedastic OLS, HC1, HC3, cluster-robust, wild cluster bootstrap, permutation - Cohort-specific ATTs (g,r)-level event-study estimates - Large-N estimators (method = "ra"/"ipw"/"ipwra") WATT(r) event study, wild cluster bootstrap, sup-t bands

title: Lee-Wooldridge Difference-in-Differences via Unit-Specific Transformations
text: Setting method "ra", "ipw", "ipwra" activates large-N path: estimates ATT(g,t) cohort period (regression adjustment, inverse-probability weighting, doubly-robust IPWRA), aggregates event-study WATT(r) path plus Pre/Post averages, reports wild cluster bootstrap standard errors simultaneous (sup-t) confidence bands. Large-N options: method, pre (pre-periods used transform), never (never-treated controls ), attgt (return ATT(g,t) cells), ydot (return transformed outcomes), reps/seed (bootstrap), level, nose. Scope. small-N path (default; Lee & Wooldridge 2026b) large-N path (method=; Lee & Wooldridge 2026a) implemented. large-N estimators (RA/IPW/IPWRA), WATT(r) aggregation, inference validated Stata lwdid v2.4.2 output lw_smoking lw_walmart (see data-raw/stata-reference/).
code: # doubly-robust IPWRA, detrending transformation, with covariates res <- lwdid(walmart, "log_wholesale_emp", "cid", "year", gvar = "first_year",              rolling = "detrend", method = "ipwra",              controls = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), reps = 999, seed = 1) print(res) plot(res)          # event-study plot with sup-t bands (requires ggplot2)

title: Lee-Wooldridge Difference-in-Differences via Unit-Specific Transformations
text: common-timing designs (gvar = NULL), supply binary post indicator. post can used two ways, lwdid() distinguishes : post treatment-indicator D_it (1 treated units post periods), ever-post units treated group — extra argument needed (backwards-compatible behavior). post calendar post indicator (1 units t ≥ first treated period), treatment group lives separate column. Pass via new dvar argument, e.g. lwdid(..., post = "post", dvar = "treated"). dvar omitted, lwdid() auto-detects unambiguous unit-invariant treat/treated/D/d column errors resolve one.

code: library(lwdidR)  # Load bundled Castle Doctrine dataset (50 US states, 2000-2010) castle <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "castle.csv", package = "lwdidR")) castle$gvar <- castle$effyear castle$gvar[is.na(castle$gvar) | castle$gvar == 0] <- NA  # Staggered design: demeaning with HC3 SEs res <- lwdid(castle, "lhomicide", "sid", "year",              gvar = "gvar", rolling = "demean", vce = "hc3") print(res) Lee-Wooldridge DiD (lwdidR) Design:      staggered Transf.:     demean VCE:         HC3 -------------------------------------------------- Overall ATT:   0.0917 SE:            0.0612 t-stat:        1.4995 p-value:       0.1376

title: Lee-Wooldridge DiD via unit-specific pre-treatment transformations — lwdid
text: data long-format panel data frame (one row per unit-period). y Character. Name outcome column. ivar Character. Name unit identifier column. tvar Character. Name calendar time column (numeric integer). gvar Character NULL. Name first-treatment-year column staggered designs. Units value 0 NA treated never-treated. Set NULL (default) common-timing designs (supply post instead). post Character NULL. Name binary post-treatment indicator column (0 = pre, 1 = post). Required gvar = NULL; ignored otherwise. dvar Character NULL. Name unit-level treatment-group indicator common-timing designs. omitted, lwdid() keeps backwards-compatible behavior post treatment-indicator; post calendar post indicator, looks unambiguous unit-invariant treatment column named treat, treated, D, d. rolling Character. Transformation method applied unit's pre-treatment observations: "demean" Subtract unit's pre-period mean (default). "detrend" Remove linear trend fitted pre-periods. "demeanq" Seasonal demeaning; requires season_var. "detrendq" Seasonal detrending; requires season_var. method Character NULL. one "ra", "ipw", "ipwra", large-N path (Lee & Wooldridge 2026a) used: per-cohort/period ATT(g,t) via regression adjustment, inverse-probability weighting, doubly-robust IPWRA, aggregated event-study WATT(r) path wild-cluster-bootstrap inference. ipw/ipwra require controls. rolling must "demean" "detrend". NULL (default), small-N path used. control_group Character. Control group staggered designs: "never_treated" (default) "not_yet_treated". aggregate Character. Aggregation level staggered designs: "overall" (default), "cohort", "none" (returns (g,r) pairs). vce Character NULL. Variance-covariance estimator: NULL (homoskedastic OLS), "hc1", "hc3", "cluster", "wildboot" (wild cluster bootstrap), "permutation" (randomisation inference). last two distribution-free recommended small N. cluster_var Character NULL. Column name clustering; required vce = "cluster". controls Character vector NULL. Names time-invariant control variables include cross-sectional regression. season_var Character NULL. Column name seasonal indicator (required rolling = "demeanq" "detrendq"). pre Integer. Large-N . Number -recent pre-periods used transformation; -1 (default) uses pre-periods. never Logical. Large-N . TRUE, comparison group never-treated units (default FALSE uses -yet-treated units ). attgt Logical. Large-N . TRUE, ATT(g,t) cell estimates returned (printed). ydot Logical. Large-N . TRUE, per-cohort transformed outcomes returned. reps Integer. Large-N . Wild cluster bootstrap replications (default 999). seed Integer NULL. Large-N . Seed wild bootstrap. level Numeric. text: Python-equivalent algorithm: cohort g: Apply transformation using pre-periods (t < g) units Compute ydot_postavg(g,) per unit Overall ATT: pooled regression Treated unit : Y_bar_i = ydot_postavg(g_i, ) Never-treated unit : Y_bar_i = sum_g w_g * ydot_postavg(g,) OLS: Y_bar ~ D (D=1 ever treated) N_treat + N_NT units Cohort ATT_g: per-cohort regression Y_bar(g,) = ydot_postavg(g,) cohort g units + NT controls OLS: Y_bar_g ~ D_g

title: lwdidR 0.2.0
text: Added large-N path Lee & Wooldridge (2026a), activated via method = "ra", "ipw", "ipwra". estimates ATT(g,t) cohort period (regression adjustment / inverse-probability weighting / doubly-robust IPWRA), aggregates event-study WATT(r) path Pre/Post averages, reports wild cluster bootstrap standard errors simultaneous (sup-t) confidence bands. New options: method, pre, never, attgt, ydot, reps, seed, level, nose. Added plot() (event-study graph via ggplot2) print()/summary() methods large-N result (class lwdid_large). Influence-function machinery ported verbatim Stata lwdid v2.4.2; large-N estimates inference validated Stata lw_smoking lw_walmart (see data-raw/stata-reference/).

title: lwdidR 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Implements Lee & Wooldridge (2026a, 2026b) estimator via unit-specific pre-treatment transformations Supports common-timing staggered adoption designs Transformation methods: demean, detrend, demeanq, detrendq Standard errors: homoskedastic OLS, HC1, HC3, cluster-robust (manual sandwich) Staggered design: overall pooled ATT, cohort-specific ATT, (g,r)-level effects Bundles Castle Doctrine dataset replication paper Section 7.2 Vignette replicating Castle Doctrine results Lee & Wooldridge (2026b) Section 7.2
